subject: Pilot billing: how long-context sessions are apportioned and minimums applied
messages:
From: Nate Harper <nate.harper@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Clarify pilot billing for long-context sessions

Hi Aisha,

Quick question as we're building our pilot: some of our clinician workflows include patient notes that are 12k+ tokens in the prompt (history + templates). Your pilot estimate assumed X tokens/session — can you confirm how Redwood bills when a single request exceeds the 16k context window and we stitch across multiple calls? Specifically: 

- Do you charge per API call strictly based on tokens sent/received, or do you apply any conversation-level minimums that would inflate costs for multi-call stitching?
- If a single logical interaction is split (prefix + followups) across two calls in the same minute, is there any aggregation or rounding applied?

We want to model expected monthly spend for the pilot (5k sessions/day peak). Any short formula or sample invoice would help.

Thanks,
Nate

Hi Nate — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: we bill per-call based on tokens (input + output) but there are a couple of platform behaviors that can affect what you see on an invoice (rounding quantum and the option for session aggregation under pilot concessions).

I'm looping in Ben (billing/math) and Marissa (pilot commercial) to give a quick worked example and confirm what we can offer for the pilot so you have a clean per-session spend estimate. From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify pilot billing for long-context sessions

Aisha / Marissa — here's the billing breakdown and a concise formula we can give Nate. I also attached a sanitized sample invoice for a comparable pilot (see attachment).

Billing model (relevant points):
- Baseline: charges are per API call = tokens_in + tokens_out, converted to token-units.
- Rounding quantum: token usage per call is rounded up to the nearest 100-token quantum for the model SKU used in this pilot (this is to keep invoice line granularity manageable).
- Minimum floor: we do not auto-apply a conversation-level minimum across separate calls by default. However, for multi-call stitching that is within a short time window and clearly part of a single logical interaction, we can apply a pilot-level aggregation so billing is calculated per logical session instead of per call. That requires an explicit concession in the pilot contract.
- Long-context overflow behavior: if input exceeds the runtime context window, customers often implement prefix-splitting. From billing POV we charge for each call after split, subject to rounding per-call unless aggregation is enabled for the session.

Worked example (numbers simplified):
- Single logical interaction: 18,500 tokens input + 1,200 tokens output total = 19,700 tokens.
- If split into two calls: Call A = 10,000 in + 600 out = 10,600 -> rounded to 10,600 -> quantum rounds up to 10,600 (already multiple of 100)
  Call B = 8,500 in + 600 out = 9,100 -> rounded up to 9,100 (nearest 100)
  Invoice tokens billed = 10,600 + 9,100 = 19,700 (same as logical total)
- But because rounding happens per-call, worst-case per-call rounding can add up. Example: if calls were 9,951 and 9,749 tokens, after 100-token rounding you'd see extra ~100+51 = 151 tokens billed vs raw total.

Pilot concession we can offer (suggested):
- For the pilot (4–8 weeks), enable session aggregation for any interaction where the customer sets a session_id and the calls are within a 2-minute window. Billing will be computed on the aggregated token total and rounded once to the 100-token quantum. This removes per-call rounding noise for high-context use-cases.
- Additionally, apply a 10% usage discount on the first 200k billed tokens to de-risk initial usage spikes.

Attachment: sample-invoice-acme-pilot.pdf (sanitized) — contains a mock invoice line showing per-call vs aggregated billing for 5 sample sessions.

If you want, I can also produce a quick spreadsheet that projects monthly spend at 5k sessions/day with/without aggregation and with the 10% concession.

— Ben
Ben Carter

This looks good. A couple of small asks / clarifications before we send to Nate: 

1) Wording: emphasize that aggregation requires a session_id and that the customer must enable consistent session_id usage (we don't retroactively aggregate without that).
2) Window: 2 minutes is reasonable; propose we offer an optional 5-minute extended window for healthcare workflows where clinicians may pause — but make it an opt-in due to higher potential abuse.
3) Discount phrasing: call it "pilot smoothing credit: 10% on first 200k billed tokens" — simpler for legal and procurement.

I'll draft the outbound email to Nate with the concise formula and the two options (2-min default, 5-min opt-in) and a note that we'll provide a sample spend spreadsheet. Also recommend we include the sample invoice as a PDF attachment.

Hi Nate — quick follow-up with concrete answers and a pilot offer.

Summary (short):
- Billing is per-call (tokens_in + tokens_out) and we apply a 100-token rounding quantum to invoice lines by default.
- Rounding can produce small per-call overhead; to avoid that for your high-context clinician flows, we can enable session aggregation for the pilot so billing is computed on the aggregated token total and rounded once. Aggregation requires that you pass a stable session_id with each related call.
- Pilot offer: "pilot smoothing credit" — 10% discount on the first 200k billed tokens + session aggregation (default 2-minute activity window; optional 5-minute window for clinical workflows if you confirm acceptable session_id discipline).

Concise formula you can use for modeling:
- If aggregation disabled: billed_tokens = sum_over_calls( round_up_to_100(tokens_in + tokens_out) )
- If aggregation enabled: billed_tokens = round_up_to_100( sum_over_session(tokens_in + tokens_out) )

Quick example (your 18.5k input + 1.2k output):
- Without aggregation (split across two calls) — small rounding delta possible (~+100–200 tokens depending on split)
- With aggregation — billed = round_up_to_100(19,700) = 19,700 (one rounding event)

Next steps:
1) If you want the session aggregation concession, confirm you will attach a consistent session_id to related calls and whether you prefer the 2-minute default or 5-minute extended window.
2) We'll send a sanitized sample invoice and a one-sheet projection at 5k sessions/day showing monthly spend with/without aggregation + pilot credit.

Attached: sample-invoice-acme-pilot.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you'd prefer us to walk through the spreadsheet live.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
